title: Load-shed new requests when TP stall detector trips (degrade replica + redirect/reject)
author: Julian Moore
description: Problem: When a TP replica is wedged (collective stall / scheduler starvation / heartbeat gap), we currently keep routing new work to it until upstream timeouts/backpressure eventually trigger. This amplifies p99, increases queue depth, and can cascade into autoscaling thrash. This PR wires the TP stall signal into overload protection so that once a replica is suspected-stalled it is immediately marked DEGRADING and stops accepting new requests; callers either get a fast, structured overload response or (when possible) are redirected to healthy replicas. Approach: 1) Introduce a "replica degraded" state driven by TP stall detector signals (from ENG-4823) with hysteresis to avoid flapping. 2) Teach the local admission controller + router to consult degraded state and load-shed before enqueue. 3) Surface a structured error code for clients and for internal retry logic, and export metrics so SRE can alert on load-shed events and correlate to heartbeat gaps. Behavior: - If tp_stall_detector trips for a replica (stall_reason != none) OR heartbeat gap exceeds threshold, set replica_state=DEGRADED for min 30s, then transition to RECOVERING once heartbeat resumes for a stable window. - While DEGRADED, admission controller rejects new requests with error_code=RUNTIME_TP_REPLICA_DEGRADED (HTTP 503 for hosted gateway, internal status for Dedicated). - Router: if other replicas for the same model+profile are healthy, redirect (internal reroute) before rejecting; otherwise fail fast to avoid unbounded queueing. - Existing in-flight requests are not force-cancelled by this change (watchdog/abort in ENG-4826 handles that path); this change only prevents pile-on. Metrics/logging: - runtime_tp_replica_degraded (gauge, labels: model, tp_degree, reason) - runtime_tp_load_shed_requests_total (counter, labels: reason, route, model) - Structured log at state transitions with replica_id, rank, reason, heartbeat_age_ms. Risk/mitigation: Primary risk is false positives causing unnecessary shedding. Mitigations: (a) hysteresis + minimum degraded window, (b) feature flag runtime.tp_load_shed_on_stall (default off in prod; enabled in canary), (c) metrics to quantify shed rate vs real stalls. Testing: Unit tests for state machine/hysteresis; integration test with simulated stall signal verifies that new requests are rejected/redirected while old requests continue (until watchdog in separate PR).

conversation: Sofia Ivanova (review): Can we ensure we don’t shed due to a single transient heartbeat miss? We’ve seen short gaps during prefill spikes. Also, what’s the ordering between scheduler backpressure vs this new degraded gate?

Julian Moore (author): Yep. The degraded transition requires either (a) stall_reason emitted (non-none) OR (b) heartbeat_age_ms > tp_stall_heartbeat_gap_ms (default 5000ms). Then we hold DEGRADED for 30s minimum and require 10s of stable heartbeat to exit. Admission controller checks DEGRADED before queueing; existing scheduler backpressure still applies after that for healthy replicas.

Rafael Mendes (SRE): +1 on fast fail. Two asks: 1) please add a counter for shed-by-reason so we can alert on sudden spikes, 2) make sure the error is actionable for on-call (points to runbook/next step).

Julian Moore (author): Added runtime_tp_load_shed_requests_total{reason=...} and structured log event runtime.replica_degraded_transition with reason + heartbeat_age_ms. Also updated error message to include "Replica degraded due to TP stall; see runbook: runtime-tp-hang-mitigation" (internal link).

Jacob Stein (review): Router reroute: are we risking request reordering or double-enqueue in race conditions? Please confirm this is pre-enqueue and idempotent. Also, how does it interact with streaming connections?

Julian Moore (author): Reroute happens before enqueue (we consult current replica state; if DEGRADED we pick next healthy candidate). There is no double-enqueue; request_id is assigned once and only enqueued on the chosen replica. For streaming: behavior is unchanged; if the initial selection is DEGRADED, we fail fast before opening stream; if it becomes DEGRADED mid-stream, this PR does nothing (watchdog/abort handles). Added a test that asserts only one enqueue occurs per request under concurrent state updates.
Aisha Bello (review): Metric naming: please align with the TP heartbeat thread (runtime_tp_* prefix). Also add tp_degree label (we page by degree/hardware).
Julian Moore (author): Renamed metrics to runtime_tp_* and added labels: model, tp_degree, route, reason. Updated docs/internal/runtime/overload-protection.md accordingly.
Sofia Ivanova (review): One more request: make the minimum degraded window configurable. Some customers may want more aggressive recovery during canary.
Julian Moore (author): Added runtime.tp_degraded_min_duration_ms and runtime.tp_degraded_recover_stable_ms under the same flag gate; defaults set conservatively. Flag remains off by default in prod.
Rafael Mendes (approval): Looks good. Please ensure rollout uses canary + Dedicated-first as per ENG-4829; otherwise OK to merge.
Julian Moore (author): Ack. Plan is to enable flag only in perf-canary + one Dedicated canary cluster; Connor coordinating under ENG-4829.

release_notes: - Runtime: when TP stall signal trips for a replica (heartbeat gap / stall reason), new requests will be load-shed (fast reject) or rerouted to healthy replicas when the feature flag runtime.tp_load_shed_on_stall is enabled. Adds metrics runtime_tp_load_shed_requests_total and runtime_tp_replica_degraded for alerting/correlation.
